races.name: bet365 Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Sony Bill
runners_data.note: Rated 140 and the class benchmark here, Harry Cobden partners a horse whose prominent style maps well to the lead in a three-runner field; recent form figures of 804-54 are mixed and similar-going record shows no wins from one placed effort, so while it controls the race shape its finishing effort is uncertain.
runners_data.comment: New connections could unlock better from Sony Bill, below his best on chase debut after a string of fencing errors at Ballinrobe — fading in the closing stages; a useful hurdler who thrives when the ground yields, he has the ability to progress over the bigger obstacles, though the mark is stiff enough.

runners_data.name: Pony Soprano
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's in-form stable (9/22 in the last 14 days) sends out a hold-up type equipped with tongue-tie who has won twice on Good ground at this sort of trip; Harry Skelton will be patient from the rear and the Good surface suits, giving this runner a strong profile for the dominant race shape.
runners_data.comment: Won here by three lengths two starts back and followed up with a solid second last time off the same mark he carries today; in fair form with a trainer at 36% and dual headgear applied for the first time — well within his compass at 2.5m and a genuine threat.

runners_data.name: Tamarind Bay
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen's six-year-old arrives on the back of a recent win just 12 days ago and has a consistent each-way record on Good and Soft, including a win over 22f on Good ground; as a hold-up horse by style, Tamarind Bay will need to produce its finish efficiently in a small field where gaps are limited, but peak fitness is a genuine edge.
runners_data.comment: Won by 16 lengths on chase debut at Stratford last time off a mark 8lb lower than today's; with his fencing career still in its early stages and suited by 2.5m on good ground, he arrives as the most unexposed runner here and rates the chief danger to the top-rated horse.

races.paceDynamic: Sony Bill is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this three-runner field and will lead from the outset, dictating a controlled, uncontested gallop over 2m4f on Good ground at Uttoxeter. With no rival willing or likely to challenge for the lead, the pace will be measured and sustainable rather than pressured, meaning Sony Bill can conserve energy through the middle stages and control the tempo into the straight. Both Pony Soprano and Tamarind Bay are hold-up types who will track at a distance and rely on a late run, but with only three runners the gaps will be minimal and the race will lack the natural compression point that helps closers generate momentum. This race shape — uncontested lead, honest gallop, small field — favours hold-up horses capable of travelling smoothly and producing a sustained finish rather than those needing a truly searching pace to unlock their best; Pony Soprano's headgear and course form and Tamarind Bay's recent win give both a viable path, but the horse that handles Good ground most fluently and travels closest to Sony Bill will be best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Stays Honest
scenarios.trigger: If Sony Bill bowls along uncontested and sets a fair, consistent gallop that keeps the closers honest throughout.
scenarios.body: If Sony Bill bowls along uncontested and sets a fair, consistent gallop that keeps the closers honest throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Sony Bill's pace proves too generous early and both hold-up horses swoop with a sustained run from two out.
scenarios.body: If Sony Bill's pace proves too generous early and both hold-up horses swoop with a sustained run from two out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sony Bill Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just slow enough that Sony Bill's jumping fluency and stamina advantage carry it clear in the home straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves just slow enough that Sony Bill's jumping fluency and stamina advantage carry it clear in the home straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jumping Error Reshuffles
scenarios.trigger: If a fencing mistake by the leader or a close-tracking rival abruptly changes the tactical picture mid-race.
scenarios.body: If a fencing mistake by the leader or a close-tracking rival abruptly changes the tactical picture mid-race.

watchPoints.text: Watch Pony Soprano's jumping from the rear — if Harry Skelton can close the gap smoothly approaching the final two fences, the horse's superior Good-ground form makes it a live threat to Sony Bill.

Sony Bill's recent form (804-54) and absence of a win on similar going from one placed effort is a flag — monitor whether Cobden asks for maximum effort early or nurses the pace, as the strategy will define the race.
Tamarind Bay's short 12-day turnaround is unusual; watch for any sign of freshness or laboured jumping early that might signal the quick return is a risk rather than a benefit.

With only three runners, the field is thin enough that a single fencing error — particularly at the open ditch — could abruptly end any horse's chance; pay attention to jumping quality in the first half of the race.

Uttoxeter's Good surface is consistent across all races today per the going report; no horse should gain or lose ground through underfoot variation, meaning pure form and tactics will be the decisive factors.

races.name: Never Ordinary At bet365 Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Flying Ace
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in two Good-ground outings over similar trips (1/20f, 1/17f), he is the only confirmed pace-setter and Harry Skelton rides for Gordon Elliott's yard which is firing at 1/26 over the past fortnight — the key horse in any pre-race assessment.
runners_data.comment: Progressive hurdler who stepped up in trip last time and ran out an 8-length winner, looking like a horse still very much on the upgrade; the distance and going are well within his compass. The weight he concedes in this small field is the only concern.

runners_data.name: Jetbob
runners_data.note: Rosemary Gasson's seven-year-old arrives 58 days fresh but boasts the most directly relevant form of the field — a win over 20f on Good ground — and travels prominently, giving him a clean run at whatever Flying Ace leaves on the table.
runners_data.comment: Dominated his hunter chase debut at Punchestown by 11 lengths last time, showing very useful form; a lightly raced point winner now switching to hurdles for a new yard, with market support likely the key indicator. The distance suits, and this type often has more to offer than the bare figures show.

runners_data.name: Not Now
runners_data.note: Nigel and Willy Twiston-Davies have had no placed runners from three runners in the past 14 days, and Not Now has been off 215 days; a hold-up type on a belated seasonal return with only two hurdling runs to his name, he needs others to do his donkey work.
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced but rated last of the five on our figures, with a well-beaten effort at Hereford in a bumper most recently; a 215-day absence adds uncertainty, and the switch to hurdling over a longer trip should help in theory. This class is a considerable ask at this stage.

runners_data.name: Way Maker
runners_data.note: Three wins from five Good-ground starts and his connections are in-form (T14: 3/12); he tracks prominently off a 26-day break which keeps him squarely involved in the early exchanges and gives James Bowen a realistic position to work from.
runners_data.comment: Dual bumper winner who found his range when stretched in trip at Southwell last time, finishing a solid 7-length second in a maiden hurdle; tops our ratings and likely to improve further with experience, the trip and sound going squarely in his favour.

runners_data.name: Moi Mon Vieux
runners_data.note: The four-year-old holds a tongue-tie, was beaten only a neck over 16f on Good ground last time, and sits at the bottom of the weights; however, his hold-up style means he is entirely dependent on the race developing into a proper test, which a single uncontested pace-setter rarely guarantees.
runners_data.comment: Solid in bumpers, finishing second at Southwell last time, and the switch to hurdling should unlock further progress from a lightly raced gelding; the going is established. The trip looks an open question given bumper form over shorter, and first-time tongue-tie is added today.

races.paceDynamic: Flying Ace is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no credible challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over this 2m4f trip on Good ground. Jetbob and Way Maker will track prominently behind, but neither is a natural pace-maker, meaning Flying Ace can set exactly the fractions he wants without being pressured into doing too much. The hold-up horses Moi Mon Vieux and Not Now will be further back, relying on Flying Ace either weakening or quickening too sharply, neither of which looks likely at a steady, self-controlled pace. This race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-lead profile — horses travelling close to Flying Ace will be best positioned when the race quickens, while late closers will have too much ground to make up against a fresh, uncontested leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Flying Ace bowls along untroubled, sets a fair gallop and quickens off the bend to score under his own terms.
scenarios.body: If Flying Ace bowls along untroubled, sets a fair gallop and quickens off the bend to score under his own terms.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Flying Ace's gallop is just strong enough to flatten him late, allowing Jetbob or Way Maker to pick him off in the final climb.
scenarios.body: If Flying Ace's gallop is just strong enough to flatten him late, allowing Jetbob or Way Maker to pick him off in the final climb.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely searching and the front two empty, giving Moi Mon Vieux or Not Now a route through late.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is genuinely searching and the front two empty, giving Moi Mon Vieux or Not Now a route through late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Jumping Errors Reshuffle
scenarios.trigger: If one or more runners makes a significant jumping error that disrupts the order and scrambles the race shape mid-race.
scenarios.body: If one or more runners makes a significant jumping error that disrupts the order and scrambles the race shape mid-race.

watchPoints.text: Flying Ace's jumping must be monitored — if Harry Skelton's mount makes a jumping error at any of the early flights it immediately opens the race up for Jetbob and Way Maker who are stalking him closely.
Way Maker's prominent position is his biggest asset; if James Bowen finds himself squeezed or blocked early on, he loses the race-shape edge his form warrants.
Not Now's 215-day absence is a genuine fitness flag — if he is ring-rusty he could capitulate quickly, but if sharp he possesses sufficient course-and-distance experience to surprise at a price.
Jetbob's 58-day gap is worth monitoring through the early stages — if he is not travelling fluently by halfway, his one-run-form reading becomes less reliable than it appears on paper.

With only five runners, the race could develop into a bunched finish from three-out; watch for Moi Mon Vieux's rider Jonathan Burke asking for an early move if he senses the pace is slowing, as sitting too far back on a small field at Uttoxeter rarely pays.

races.name: bet365 Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Gunsight Ridge
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner taking on a leadership role here; Good-going form is limited (2 runs, one place) and he carries top weight of 168lbs, but the uncontested lead is his to take and over 2m his stamina concerns are reduced — style fit is high for the position he will actually occupy.
runners_data.comment: Third at this course on his latest start, Gunsight Ridge has been below his best this season but has slipped down the weights and hinted at a return to form last time; he can be sluggish in his racing, but the first-time tongue-tie may help address that and he handles today's trip and ground well.

runners_data.name: Breaking Cover
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a strong Good-ground record (3W 6P from 7 runs) and multiple wins over this 2m trip; 225 days off the track is the key query for Anthony Honeyball's yard, but Sam Twiston-Davies' booking and a premium Good-ground profile make him a natural fit for the prominent-tracking scenario.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his recent sequence before an extended absence and a run in a Grade 2 last time where he was outclassed on unsuitable ground; returning to handicap company at 2m on good ground is more his sphere, though 225 days off needs overcoming and the current weight could prove stiff.

runners_data.name: Newtown Rambler
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in his last two runs both over 2m, including a win at this distance on Good going just 21 days ago under the same Oakley Brown (5) partnership; the tongue-tie is retained and his in-form profile for Keatley's yard (3/15 last 14 days) makes him a potent force in the prominent group.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last five starts, going boldly at the front and landing a handicap last time by five lengths; today's ground should suit, but the revised mark represents a significant hike from his winning base and dual headgear applied for the first time suggests connections have questions at the current level.

runners_data.name: Coastguard Station
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse whose best form (2nd twice in last three) has come on Good ground over 2m-plus trips; dropping back to 2m is a potential concern as he tends to finish strongly from off a genuine pace — Henry Oliver yard in form (1/1 last 14 days) is a positive angle.
runners_data.comment: Second at Fakenham last time under more forward tactics, Coastguard Station is in fair form and handles this trip and ground well; first-time cheekpieces suggest connections are refining his approach, and he is well respected on our figures despite being winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Sir Tivo
runners_data.note: Veteran of 12 years and a natural hold-up or rear-of-prominent type who has placed five times on Good ground; wins tend to come over shorter trips (15f) on Good, and James Bowen's booking suits a horse who needs clean jumping ahead of him rather than a falsely-run contest.
runners_data.comment: Back in form after a revival at a sharp track last time, Sir Tivo is at his best when allowed to bowl along at 2m on good ground; on the same mark as when beaten 2.5 lengths last time with dual headgear applied for the first time, he is a solid danger — though inconsistency has been a theme.

runners_data.name: Kingston Narcissus
runners_data.note: In-form horse with back-to-back wins including a Good-ground success over 2m — though naturally prominent, he is effectively displaced in this map because Gunsight Ridge takes the position he would ideally want; his 11-day turnaround under Harry Skelton for the powerful Dan Skelton yard is a legitimate positive, even if he cannot fully express his front-running instinct.
runners_data.comment: Won by 17 lengths two starts back before a close-up second last time on the same mark he carries today; the trainer is firing at 55% and his underlying chase form marks him out as well treated — the one to beat in this seven-runner field.

runners_data.name: Gris Majeur
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 2m on Good ground and is clearly in form for Sheila Lewis, but as a true hold-up type he faces the challenge that the race shape here offers little genuine pace to aim at; Sean Houlihan rides and the horse's strong finishing profile is partially undermined by the controlled tempo that is expected.
runners_data.comment: Won at Bangor last time by over four lengths in a race where the leaders set a strong pace, suiting his hold-up style; handles a wide range of trips and ground and arrives in fair form, though our figures place him last of seven and this is a considerably stronger heat.

races.paceDynamic: Gunsight Ridge is the confirmed pace-setter and will lead from the front in what is essentially a lone-speed scenario over 2m at Uttoxeter on Good ground. With no genuine challenger to push him early, he sets a controlled, sustainable tempo that keeps the race together and limits the scope for a late sprint finish. The field holds more prominent-minded horses than the map can accommodate — Kingston Narcissus and Gris Majeur are both naturally forward-going but are displaced to midfield in reality, meaning the race shape is tidier at the front than the raw numbers suggest. This controlled pace over a sharp 2m strongly favours horses who travel prominently, jump cleanly, and can produce a sharp effort from the second-last fence rather than pure hold-up gallopers relying on a true end-to-end test.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Gunsight Ridge dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and the winner comes from prominent tracking positions.
scenarios.body: If Gunsight Ridge dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and the winner comes from prominent tracking positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Gunsight Ridge jumps immaculately and the pace is so controlled that no challenger can close the gap in the final two fences.
scenarios.body: If Gunsight Ridge jumps immaculately and the pace is so controlled that no challenger can close the gap in the final two fences.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is faster than expected and the front rank tire in the final half-mile, leaving a late closer to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is faster than expected and the front rank tire in the final half-mile, leaving a late closer to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Jumping Errors Disrupt Shape
scenarios.trigger: If multiple jumping mistakes scramble the race order and the outcome is decided by who survives rather than who has the superior tactical position.
scenarios.body: If multiple jumping mistakes scramble the race order and the outcome is decided by who survives rather than who has the superior tactical position.

watchPoints.text: Breaking Cover's 225-day absence is the single biggest risk factor in the race — watch for any sign of rustiness at the start or hesitancy at the early fences that could compromise his prominent position.

Kingston Narcissus cannot fully access his natural front-running role with Gunsight Ridge already committed to the lead — watch whether Harry Skelton elects to press or drop him in, as that decision will materially alter the pace shape in the final mile.

Newtown Rambler carries an amateur claim (Oakley Brown, 5lb) and has run twice in 21 days; watch for any sign of fatigue or a drop in jumping fluency as the race develops, which would undermine his otherwise strong form profile.

Gris Majeur and Coastguard Station are both held-up horses in a race with only one genuine pace-setter — if Gunsight Ridge slows dramatically or makes a jumping error, these two are most likely to benefit from any resulting late-race scramble.

Good ground is confirmed across the card at Uttoxeter and all seven runners are rated OK for going — no ground-related withdrawals expected, so the race will run to its predicted shape without significant last-minute disruption.

races.name: bet365 Summer Cup Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Hang In There
runners_data.note: 12-year-old veteran who won over C&D on Good and gets a soft lead here; visor-fitted and capable front-runner but age and 55-day absence are mild flags on jumping reliability over 3m.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Fakenham last time, Hang In There heads our figures and handles today's trip and ground; a fresh campaign alongside a first-time visor makes him the one to beat, though the mark is stiff enough that a sharp performance will be needed.

runners_data.name: Riskintheground
runners_data.note: Dual recent winner in good form (1-2-1 last three), Harry Skelton aboard for the in-form Skelton yard; genuine hold-up style suits a test scenario but 3m on Good requires the pace to truly stretch for him to close.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last three starts, including a narrow victory last time under a patient ride that confirmed he stays 2m7f; with the trainer in excellent form and a first-time tongue-tie applied, he is a serious danger here — though the revised mark may be at the ceiling of his ability.

runners_data.name: Twig
runners_data.note: Beau Morgan (5) takes over from the saddle; two Good-ground wins in his last five including a 3m success, and prominent style means he should secure a natural position tracking Hang In There throughout.
runners_data.comment: Two wins earlier in his recent sequence underline his ability when conditions suit, and today's 3m on good ground is right in his range; first-time cheekpieces could sharpen him up after a well-beaten effort at Bangor last time, though the mark may prove a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Alien Storm
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with two wins on Good at similar trips; David Bass keeps the ride and his Good-ground record (11 runs, 2W 9P) underlines his comfort with today's conditions.
runners_data.comment: Solid form at shorter trips with two wins in his recent sequence, but outstayed over a longer distance at Bangor last time despite moving through the race with purpose; today's 3m appears near the limits of his stamina on good ground, making this a test, though competitive enough off his current weight.

runners_data.name: Ki Woo
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with progressive profile, won over 3m2f on Good last time; Jack Tudor aboard and hg:tp headgear worn — young for the grade but well-placed in the field and may get the rails berth.
runners_data.comment: A winner at Cartmel last time by over three lengths, Ki Woo is making steady progress over fences and stays well beyond today's trip; first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces are a new combination, though the mark is a step up on what he has faced in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Peaky Boy
runners_data.note: Back-to-back third-place finishes on Good recently suggest consistency without a finishing kick; hg:tp, prominent style, but hasn't won since mid-campaign and may fill a minor-placing role again.
runners_data.comment: Back in form with consecutive thirds in his last two starts, Peaky Boy handles any ground and the 2.5-3m range suits him well; first-time headgear may sharpen his response, but he remains winless in his recent runs and the current mark is a steep ask.

runners_data.name: Hold Your Fort
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator with three wins on Good; Callum Pritchard (conditional) takes the ride for small yard — 55 days off and trainer with no 14-day runners, but recent course form reads 3-2-1 on Good.
runners_data.comment: Steadily progressive over this trip on fast ground, Hold Your Fort won by over five lengths three starts back before struggling to dictate terms when third last time out; 1lb lower here after a short break, but our figures place him firmly in the outsider bracket.

runners_data.name: Queensbury Boy
runners_data.note: Won over 2m5f on Good last time, prominent style; Mickey Bowen's yard in strong form (T14: 3/12) and James Bowen aboard — may need to find a way through traffic if shuffled back.
runners_data.comment: Second by a neck last time off his current mark, Queensbury Boy ranks equal-top on our figures on the back of strong hurdle form; today's 3m tests his stamina limits and jumping over fences has been inconsistent — the main reservation, alongside the first-time tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Time To Bite
runners_data.note: Bryan Carver partners a horse with seven wins on Good and strong prominent instincts; forced wide of his natural berth in this congested field, his STYLE_FIT flag means he is unlikely to reproduce best if unable to get forward early.
runners_data.comment: A front-runner who won at Fakenham two starts back, Time To Bite has been thriving, but he was outstayed last time when used too aggressively; first-time blinkers aim to address that tendency, though our figures rank him last of the 13 runners.

runners_data.name: Grand Clermont
runners_data.note: David Pipe's 10-year-old won last time out and has been placed at this track; amateur Mr Lucas Murphy (7) takes a big-field handicap ride, but this horse's natural front-running tendency will be squeezed in this shape and his recent Good-ground strike-rate (3 runs, 1W 2P) is modest.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last five starts including an 18-length success at this track two starts back, Grand Clermont still appears well treated on his combined UK and French form; 2lb higher than when runner-up last time but a first-time tongue-tie and the right conditions give him solid claims.

runners_data.name: Samuel Spade
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's seven-year-old most recently won over 2m3f on Good and brings fresh hold-up energy; Ben Jones rides and his last-time-out win shows he's in form, a live option if the pace produces a true test.
runners_data.comment: A useful performer over hurdles now applying that talent to fences, Samuel Spade landed his handicap chase debut at Worcester last time by two and a half lengths; still building his jumping technique and effective at 2.5-3m, he has scope for further progress in this sphere.

runners_data.name: Regarde
runners_data.note: Strong place record on Good (four places from ten runs) and a natural front-runner; Gavin Sheehan partners but this horse's tendency to want a prominent pitch is compromised in this field, making a midfield berth against his grain.
runners_data.comment: Finishing well from the rear at Aintree last time, beaten three lengths, Regarde handles 3m+ on good ground and connections landed this prize last year; blinkers first time may help, but without a win in his last four starts he remains an outsider on our figures.

runners_data.name: Imperial Alex
runners_data.note: Stan Sheppard partners Tom Lacey's nine-year-old who won over 3m on Good last time; naturally wants to race forward but will be crowded out of that position, meaning his effort will depend on finding a clear run from an unnatural mid-group position.
runners_data.comment: Back in form with a win at Stratford last time, landing a handicap on a step up in trip by two and a quarter lengths; first-time cheekpieces are a new addition and he handles 3m on a sound surface, though our figures place him in the outsider bracket for this stronger contest.

runners_data.name: Stratagem
runners_data.note: Listed as NON-RUNNER — if declared, Mickey Bowen's prominent-style 10-year-old has a fine record on Good over staying trips (3W on Good in last five) but faces the same overcrowding issue as other prominent types in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Hang In There is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, will dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 3m trip on Good ground at Uttoxeter. The field is unusually congested with prominent-style horses — Time To Bite, Grand Clermont, Regarde, Imperial Alex and Stratagem are all natural front-to-mid runners who will be compressed into midfield because Hang In There and the core prominent quartet of Twig, Alien Storm, Ki Woo and Peaky Boy will fill the early positions. With one horse controlling an honest but unforced pace, this sets up as a test of jumping fluency and stamina from the front, with the race likely to be decided by those who travel prominently without burning their fuel. This race shape most favours horses with a prominent or pressing style who can track the steady pace, jump well and quicken from 3-out — true hold-up horses face an uphill task closing on a sound surface at a controlled tempo. The field holds more prominent-running types than the race shape can accommodate, with Hang In There, Twig, Alien Storm, Ki Woo and Peaky Boy the most likely to actually secure their preferred early positions; Time To Bite, Grand Clermont, Regarde, Imperial Alex and Stratagem will be shuffled back against their nature.

scenarios.title: Hang In There Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Hang In There is allowed to dictate an uncontested lead and jumps cleanly throughout.
scenarios.body: If Hang In There is allowed to dictate an uncontested lead and jumps cleanly throughout.

scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Picks Off Leader Late
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent tracker travels powerfully through the race and produces a clean jump at the last to collar Hang In There.
scenarios.body: If a prominent tracker travels powerfully through the race and produces a clean jump at the last to collar Hang In There.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Strongly
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly stronger than expected and the field strings out, leaving a gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: If the pace is slightly stronger than expected and the field strings out, leaving a gap for a late finisher.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Field Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded prominent group causes interference, loose horses, or multiple fallers that scramble the result.
scenarios.body: If the overcrowded prominent group causes interference, loose horses, or multiple fallers that scramble the result.

watchPoints.text: Hang In There is 12 years old returning after 55 days — watch his jumping from the third-last where tiring veteran chasers most often make costly errors at Uttoxeter.

The prominent group of Twig, Ki Woo, Alien Storm and Peaky Boy will all seek the same early positions; watch for crowding and interference at the first three fences that could compromise several market principals.

Riskintheground is a genuine hold-up horse but Uttoxeter's flat Good track reduces late-run opportunities — watch whether Harry Skelton sends him forward earlier than expected to compensate for the controlled pace.

Time To Bite and Grand Clermont are both natural front-runners redistributed to midfield; watch whether either jockey (Carver or Murphy) overrides the instruction and forces forward, which could unexpectedly quicken the early gallop and destabilise the race shape.

Samuel Spade won last time over a shorter trip on Good — watch whether Ben Jones attempts to position him more prominently than his hold-up tag suggests, given the Good surface and 3m trip that suit a positive ride.

races.name: bet365 Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Blizzard Of Oz
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner whose natural prominent style is confirmed; Good ground suits its sim-going record (1W3P in 6 runs) and the uncontested lead over 2m7½f flatters its chance, though the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) indicates it is stretching slightly beyond its comfort zone in this role — treat as pace anchor rather than banker.
runners_data.comment: Persistent jumping errors and inconsistency make him a difficult proposition, and he burned himself out too soon at Ballinrobe last time. The trip and going pose no problems, but he's ranked bottom of this field on our figures.

runners_data.name: Bold Endeavour
runners_data.note: Veteran of 10 who wants to race prominently; 50-day absence and a winless sim-going record (0W1P from 5) are concerns, though it handles Good and will track the leader over this stamina-test trip for trainer Chris Honour.
runners_data.comment: Third on our ratings and carrying a mark that flatters on his best form, but inconsistency has been his downfall — a succession of jumping errors at Haydock last time left him well beaten. The trip and ground suit, and he's a threat if he settles and jumps cleanly.

runners_data.name: Crebilly
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse ridden by the in-form Harry Cobden; won last time out over 2m on Good and now steps up to 2m7½f which his breeding and style strongly support — just two sim-going runs from 15 is a minor flag but recent form is excellent.
runners_data.comment: Back to form last time, winning off a reduced mark at Market Rasen with nothing to spare; still well placed on his best form despite the 4lb rise, and first-time cheekpieces are a positive addition. The main query is whether he'll see out this longer trip.

runners_data.name: American Sniper
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with the deepest Good-ground form in the field (8 runs, 2W3P) and two wins at this trip range; Rian Corcoran's 5lb claim is a bonus, and a tongue-tie is in place — the consistent placed form at 19-22f marks him as a genuine player over this longer trip.
runners_data.comment: Front-runner who thrives when allowed to control his own pace, and he bolted up by 13 lengths at Newton Abbot last time off a reduced mark; still on a manageable figure, with distance and going well established. The step back up in class is the key test.

runners_data.name: Gabbys Cross
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has finished placed twice in recent Good-ground outings; at 11 years old stamina holds but class may be declining, and a 64-day break adds a fitness question — Jack Tudor is a positive booking.
runners_data.comment: Second on our ratings and well rated against his best Irish form, with connections having been successful in this race last year; probably found the trip a stretch at Sandown most recently. Consistent form on a sound surface would make him a serious threat.

runners_data.name: Musique De Fee
runners_data.note: Front-of-field type with outstanding Good-ground figures (12 runs, 3W9P) and consistent placed form over 26f; tongue-tie retained and trainer Mickey Bowen has struck at 25% over 14 days — the trip is a slight stretch at 2m7½f but the going suits perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Front-running style suits this trip and surface, and the mark remains achievable on earlier form, but she pulled up at Cartmel last time; twin headgear changes — first-time blinkers and tongue-tie — signal connections trying a new approach, and she needs to rediscover recent consistency.

runners_data.name: Ebony Warrior
runners_data.note: Strong Good-ground performer (3W5P from 8 relevant runs) whose natural front-end style means it has been pushed into a midfield map slot it would not choose — the crowded prominent group makes securing its favoured position unlikely, and the resulting energy cost could blunt its finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Back to form at Worcester last time, winning by 3 lengths off a reduced mark and confirming his stamina for this kind of trip; still generously weighted against his best form, and first-time tongue-tie is a small addition. The step up in class after a quick turnaround is the main risk.

runners_data.name: Miss Goldfire
runners_data.note: Four wins from 10 Good-ground starts give her a strong surface profile, but this mare naturally wants to race forward and with the prominent berths oversubscribed, settling mid-division is a real possibility that would compromise her usual race pattern.
runners_data.comment: Coasted home by 11 lengths at Newton Abbot last time, clearly flourishing with the step up in trip; retains a fair mark on her best form even after the rise, and first-time tongue-tie is the only change. Bigger fields may test her consistency.

runners_data.name: Escapologist
runners_data.note: Has the form to be competitive (three Good-ground wins) and travels best when prominent, but the field density means he is likely to be shuffled back — headgear (tp) suggests a horse that needs mental freshness as much as tactical position, and racing out of role is a genuine concern.
runners_data.comment: Consistent enough, with a decent third at Plumpton last time behind him, and the trip and ground are well within his compass; first-time tongue-tie suggests connections see more to come. Our figures, however, rank him near the foot of this field, making him difficult to endorse.

runners_data.name: My Gift To You
runners_data.note: The most prolific Good-ground horse in the field (4W7P from 13 runs) with a recent win at 33f; Jonathan Burke is an astute pilot who may well manoeuvre him into a forward slot ahead of expectations, making him the most dangerous of the five redistributed prominent types if that plan succeeds.
runners_data.comment: Twin headgear changes — tongue-tie and visor for the first time — reflect connections seeking an answer, as he went too hard in front at Cartmel last time and faded; remains consistent over the trip and going, though the handicapper has a firm grip on his ceiling.

runners_data.name: Oakley
runners_data.note: Progressive in recent form (123 in last five includes wins and places) and handles Good ground well (2W8P); naturally prominent but likely to find the race real estate crowded early — if reshuffled, the 22-day turnaround at least means he arrives fresh.
runners_data.comment: Third last time off a mark 1lb higher than today, and generally in decent recent form; won well at Hereford three starts back off a more lenient figure, but this longer trip looks a stretch. Our figures place him near the foot of this field.

races.paceDynamic: Blizzard Of Oz is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to press it, should slot into an uncontested lead and control tempo over this 2m7½f trip on Good ground. The field is saturated with prominent-type riders — Ebony Warrior, Miss Goldfire, Escapologist, My Gift To You and Oakley all want to race forward but cannot all occupy those positions, so several will be shuffled back into unnatural midfield slots where their STYLE_FIT tags signal a meaningful discount. Bold Endeavour and Gabbys Cross are legitimate front-of-field types who will fill the chasing roles behind the leader, meaning a structured, moderate gallop through the first half is the likeliest outcome, with the race coming alive from three out. This shape — a lone leader setting a controlled, honest pace over a staying trip on a sound surface — most favours genuine hold-up horses who travel fluently before producing a sustained late run, giving Crebilly and American Sniper the profile edge over the crowded prominent pack.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Blizzard Of Oz Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Blizzard Of Oz leads at a measured pace and the reshuffled prominent runners fail to mount early pressure, leaving the race to develop from the home turn.
scenarios.body: If Blizzard Of Oz leads at a measured pace and the reshuffled prominent runners fail to mount early pressure, leaving the race to develop from the home turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely modest and the true hold-up horses save ground before unleashing a strong finish from three out.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves genuinely modest and the true hold-up horses save ground before unleashing a strong finish from three out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Bold Endeavour or Gabbys Cross press Blizzard Of Oz from halfway, turning it into a stamina test that cracks the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: If Bold Endeavour or Gabbys Cross press Blizzard Of Oz from halfway, turning it into a stamina test that cracks the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Reshuffled Prominent Breaks Free
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed prominent horses (Ebony Warrior, Miss Goldfire or My Gift To You) secures an early position ahead of expectations and travels on the leader's girth throughout.
scenarios.body: If one of the redistributed prominent horses (Ebony Warrior, Miss Goldfire or My Gift To You) secures an early position ahead of expectations and travels on the leader's girth throughout.

watchPoints.text: Blizzard Of Oz sets the pace alone — if Jack O'Neill is allowed to control tempo from the front without interference, any horse that gets into a prominent tracking position early (particularly My Gift To You or Gabbys Cross) will have a race-deciding advantage over rivals stuck in traffic.

The five redistributed prominent horses (Ebony Warrior, Miss Goldfire, Escapologist, My Gift To You, Oakley) will contest the same two or three early positions — watch for crowding and potential shuffling at the first hurdle that could compromise several fancied runners simultaneously.

Musique De Fee's trainer Mickey Bowen has a sharp 14-day strike rate (3/12); if this horse is saddled with any market move, the stable confidence angle may outweigh the slightly inadequate 2m7½f trip.

Crebilly's headgear note (p — hood presumably) and the step up from 2m to 2m7½f is the key stamina unknown — Harry Cobden's judgment of how far to send him back early will determine whether the trip brings out the best or exposes a limit.

American Sniper carries a tongue-tie (tb) and is the only runner with multiple wins specifically on Good ground at distances of 19-22f — watch whether Rian Corcoran (5lb claimer) settles him in the sweet spot at the rear of the first division.

races.name: Bet Boost At bet365 Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Morning Mayhem
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield's 5yo goes fresh enough (16 days) having won twice over this course-and-distance profile, but the STYLE_FIT tag flags she is effectively racing in a lead role that sits just outside her natural prominent style — her 1W2P similar-going record is respectable but not dominant, and all eyes are on whether she can sustain control solo.
runners_data.comment: Generally progressive and capable of winning by wide margins at his best, Morning Mayhem was not seen to best advantage when stepped up in trip last time; back at 2m on good ground is more suitable, though he carries 1lb more than when fourth last time and ranks lowest on our figures here.

runners_data.name: Hope Rising
runners_data.note: Jamie Snowden's hold-up specialist boasts an outstanding similar-going record of 13/15 (3W7P) and has finished placed in four of five recent starts, making her easily the most ground-consistent horse in the race — the concern is purely whether Morning Mayhem's likely leisurely gallop generates enough pace for her late charge to fire.
runners_data.comment: Beaten just a length at Stratford last time after being detached behind an early front-runner, Hope Rising is consistent and well suited by 2m on fast ground; she rates a strong danger here and the manner of that effort suggests her ability is not fully exposed at this level.

runners_data.name: Edelak
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners this Dan Skelton 4yo, who has won three of her last four and is fresh on 12 days' rest — she wears a hood and her strong Good-ground record (7/9) suggests conditions are ideal, though her STYLE_FIT flag means she may end up tracking closer than is entirely natural rather than pressing the leader as aggressively as her style suggests.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins, the latest an emphatic 28-length success at Stratford on his handicap debut, mark Edelak out as progressive with more to offer; the trainer is operating at 52%, first-time cheekpieces add an intriguing element and today's conditions look ideal — comfortably the one to beat in this small field.

runners_data.name: Caelan
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's hold-up 5yo returns after 44 days wearing a tongue-tie on a track where he has placed twice at 16f on Good ground, but his complete absence of wins from six similar-going runs (0W2P) and a claim jockey (Lewis Saunders, 5lb) make him the most dependent on race conditions falling perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer who handles 2m on good to soft ground, Caelan was beaten 11 lengths at Aintree last time on a demanding track; a first-time tongue-tie may help sharpen him, though he is yet to win in his last five starts and the trainer is below peak at 29% lately.

races.paceDynamic: Morning Mayhem is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of four, and with no rival willing to dispute the lead, she will dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo around Uttoxeter's 2m hurdle course on Good ground. Edelak is a prominent racer who may press or track closely, but with a STYLE_FIT flag she is operating slightly outside her most natural role and may not exert genuine pressure on the pace. Hope Rising and Caelan are both hold-up types who will be positioned at the rear, reliant on the pace being truly honest and the leader tying herself up — which is unlikely with no pressure applied. The dominant race shape heavily favours a prominent or pace-tracking runner who can sit just off Morning Mayhem and pounce at the final flight, rather than a deep closer who needs genuine end-to-end gallop to close the gap.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Morning Mayhem bowls along at her own tempo, conserves energy, and the hold-up horses cannot generate enough late momentum on Good ground.
scenarios.body: If Morning Mayhem bowls along at her own tempo, conserves energy, and the hold-up horses cannot generate enough late momentum on Good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Edelak tracks Morning Mayhem closely throughout and produces a fluent jumping display to collar her between the last two flights.
scenarios.body: If Edelak tracks Morning Mayhem closely throughout and produces a fluent jumping display to collar her between the last two flights.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely brisk enough for Hope Rising or Caelan to deliver a sweeping late run from the rear.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely brisk enough for Hope Rising or Caelan to deliver a sweeping late run from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If Morning Mayhem makes a critical jumping error or the pace proves too hot early, triggering a scrambled finish.
scenarios.body: If Morning Mayhem makes a critical jumping error or the pace proves too hot early, triggering a scrambled finish.

watchPoints.text: Morning Mayhem's jumping accuracy will be critical — a mistake at any of the early flights could instantly gift Edelak or Hope Rising the initiative in a small field where there is no safety net.

Hope Rising's hold-up style requires a genuine gallop; if Morning Mayhem dawdles, watch for Gavin Sheehan taking a closer position than expected to ensure he does not get left flat-footed at the business end.

Edelak's hood (headgear flag) and recent quick turnaround (12 days) need monitoring in the paddock — if she is free early and over-jumps in front, she could run keenly and burn out before the final climb.

With only four runners, any early incident or jumping blunder will have an outsized effect on race shape — a false start or unseated rider at the first would dramatically alter the dynamics Scenario A depends upon.
Caelan's trainer Olly Murphy has returned just 1/7 in the last 14 days — low strike rate tempers expectations for this runner in what is already an uphill task from off the pace.

races.name: Best Odds Guaranteed At bet365 Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ocean Conquest
runners_data.note: A 5yo prominent racer with a win on Good at 21f; 88 days off is the main query but Nigel & Willy Twiston-Davies send him fit enough and Sam Twiston-Davies has strong course familiarity — p headgear fitted and form figures show he is best fresh on a fair surface.
runners_data.comment: Fresh after an 88-day absence and well within range of today's trip — the extended 3m at Southwell last time found him out; first-time cheekpieces add a stimulus. A sequence of below-par efforts asks questions, though a more suitable distance gives grounds for optimism.

runners_data.name: Kom Tu Voudras
runners_data.note: The race's only genuine front-runner, Harry Cobden takes the ride for an in-form Faye Bramley stable (2 wins from 8 in 14 days); recent 1-2-1 sequence on Good and Heather ground, tp headgear, and just 17 days since last run all point to peak fitness.
runners_data.comment: Thriving in handicap company, landing a race at Worcester last time when ridden with confidence at a testing track; lightly raced with more improvement likely now settling into this sphere. The twin headgear additions — tongue-tie and cheekpieces for the first time — are the only query.

runners_data.name: Gardener
runners_data.note: A 10yo hold-up type who does his best work from the rear; Charlie Maggs (3) takes over and the horse has two Good-ground wins at 20f — soft-ground limitations are less relevant here, but age and consistent form figures of 3-3-1-1 suggest he is a consistent rather than explosive finisher.
runners_data.comment: Front-runner who landed a tight finish at Hexham two starts back, though performed to his recent level without threatening at the same mark last time; the trip and ground are familiar, and first-time tongue-tie is a small addition. His best suggests this mark is still workable.

runners_data.name: Ballygeary
runners_data.note: Form figures of 6-7-3-6-5 tell a modest story in this company, and while he is a true hold-up horse by nature, the crowded rear means he is unlikely to secure his ideal position — William Maggs (3) will need a strong pace to set things up, which is not guaranteed under this front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Out of form in recent starts, comfortably held at Southwell last time; the trip and going present no issues and first-time tongue-tie is a change. Yet to win in his last five starts, and there is little encouragement from the current run of results.

runners_data.name: Sun Joy
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's 7yo is a reliable prominent racer with five top-two finishes in recent Good-ground races including this trip; 18 days since last run and an in-form trainer (1/3 in 14 days) make him a live threat to sit close enough to Kom Tu Voudras and challenge at the business end.
runners_data.comment: Clearly in good order, finishing 4 lengths second at Fontwell last time in a race run over a shorter trip than his best; stepping back up in distance today with the going to suit, and the current mark still generous on his best efforts. First-time tongue-tie is the only addition.

runners_data.name: Suttons Hill
runners_data.note: 419 days off (with a pull-up on the comeback attempt 35 days ago noted in the form) is a serious fitness flag; Joe Anderson (3) partners a horse whose best form came over shorter trips on Good, and the lengthy absence plus a poor recent p/u rating make this an obvious risk even if the price tempts.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of our ratings in this field, with a recent pull-up in a point and still needing to demonstrate his worth under rules; effective over two to two-and-a-half miles, and first-time hood is a gear change. Hard to make a convincing case here.

runners_data.name: Dream's Ka
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners Dan Skelton's 4yo, the combination's 9/22 in 14 days showing strong stable form; Dream's Ka races from hold-up and has four Good-ground runs showing a 2-1-2-7 sequence — young, lightly raced, and likely to improve, he is the most potent late-runner in this field if pace develops.
runners_data.comment: Top-rated on our figures with a trainer in fine current form; he travelled well last time, hit the front but was outstayed late when a narrow second off a mark 3lb lower than today, while two starts back he cleared away more decisively when conditions fully favoured. Stamina is the only mild query.

runners_data.name: Hello Cello
runners_data.note: Harry Fry's 7yo is a genuine come-from-behind type who won on Soft and has been placed on Good; Ciaran O'Shea (7) gets the ride for a trainer with no runners in the last 14 days, and 55 days off adds a fitness query — with the rear positions crowded, the horse is forced to race closer than ideal and that blunts its natural profile.
runners_data.comment: Third at Warwick last time, probably hitting the front a touch too soon when stepping up in trip but staying on creditably; the trip and going suit her profile, and first-time tongue-tie is added today. Our figures place her near the foot of the field.

races.paceDynamic: Kom Tu Voudras is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Harry Cobden in the saddle and a healthy recent record, will stride straight to the front and set a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m4f trip on Good ground. Ocean Conquest, Sun Joy, and Suttons Hill are all prominent-style runners who will push for early position behind the leader, meaning the front end will not be entirely uncontested but Kom Tu Voudras is unlikely to be seriously pressured into an unsustainable pace. Dream's Ka is the most naturally placed hold-up horse with a genuine rear-to-midfield profile and a strong finishing thread, while Gardener operates from deep too. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can place at the rear — Ballygeary and Hello Cello are true come-from-behind horses pushed into midfield slots on the map because there are simply too many for the rear positions, meaning their chances in a shape that requires a true late run are somewhat compromised. This race shape — a controlled pace set by one clear front-runner with a chasing pack sitting close — most favours a horse that can travel prominently and produce a clean jump-for-jump finish, or a genuine hold-up horse with a strong turn of foot if the pace proves honest enough to set things up from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kom Tu Voudras Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Kom Tu Voudras leads uncontested at a fair but manageable gallop and the prominent chasers fail to close the gap at the second-last.
scenarios.body: If Kom Tu Voudras leads uncontested at a fair but manageable gallop and the prominent chasers fail to close the gap at the second-last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is honest enough to stretch Kom Tu Voudras and a prominent or mid-positioned horse arrives with a sustained run from the second-last.
scenarios.body: If the gallop is honest enough to stretch Kom Tu Voudras and a prominent or mid-positioned horse arrives with a sustained run from the second-last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack sets a genuinely strong tempo that burns out the front-runner and creates enough daylight for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: If the prominent pack sets a genuinely strong tempo that burns out the front-runner and creates enough daylight for a late finisher.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Creates Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the race breaks down tactically — leader checked, scrimmaging in the early stages, or prominent horses overcommitting — handing a long-shot an uncontested lead.
scenarios.body: If the race breaks down tactically — leader checked, scrimmaging in the early stages, or prominent horses overcommitting — handing a long-shot an uncontested lead.

watchPoints.text: Kom Tu Voudras — Harry Cobden could choose to inject pace at any point; if he builds a substantial advantage at the top of the straight, the prominent chasers may simply have too much ground to make up.

Ocean Conquest — 88 days off for a 5yo carrying headgear; watch the market for any significant move that suggests the yard has given the horse a quiet prep, as a flat run from a long layoff could reshape the whole race.

Suttons Hill — 419-day absence and a pull-up 35 days ago make him an unpredictable participant; a jumping error or early exit from this runner could interfere with the midfield pack and disrupt the race shape.

Ballygeary and Hello Cello — both are true hold-up horses forced into midfield by the crowded rear; if either drops back to their natural position from the start, the actual pace map in-running will differ from projections and could compress the chasing pack.

Dream's Ka — at just 4 years old this is still a developing jumper; any hesitation at a hurdle could cost him the race-long momentum he needs to produce his finish, so watch his jumping in the first half of the race.
